messages.subject: Plant height estimation
parts:
Hello Filipe and colleagues,

I would like to know if it is possible to estimate the height of plants using the difference between the canopy height of the plot and the height of the soil around the plot.

Unfortunately in this trial, I had no way to fly to get the soil base. However, as it is possible to observe the soil around the plot well, I believe that it may be possible to make an estimate with the soil-canopy difference within the plot.

I'm sharing the link with the orthomosaic and DEM, I cut them to reduce the file size.

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bsY7rC-uccfazbPhssi8NrQZnt0Dx5U7?usp=sharing

Thank you.

Cleber

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: FIELDimageR: Plant height estimation
parts:
Hi Cleber and Gustavo,

I like Gustavo's suggestion. That's a great approach for annual crops and for calculating directly the Canopy Height Model (CHM). Another possibility is (1) use fieldMask() to remove plants instead of soil. (2) Then uses the $mask output as a mask on the DSM file to eliminate plant area and (3) evaluate only the average height of soil per plot.

Normally the plant height pipeline is (1) making the mask to remove soil using RGB mosaic; (2) using the mask on DSM mosaic to eliminate soil; and (3) evaluating plant height per plot. Once that you are able to see the soil in the images the suggestion is to do the same pipeline described above, however eliminating plants beside soil in the first stage. In this case, you won't be able to calculate the CHM (canopy height model) once that you do not have soil values for pixels with plants. You will be able to calculate an approximation by extracting values per plot with plants and with soil and making the difference in the final value afterwords. 

Does it make sense?

Hope it works... Let me know if you guys have any other suggestions.

Best,
Filipe

Hello Guys,

I did some tests and it worked pretty well. The plant height estimates make a lot of sense, I've checked it only in a few plots, to adjust the script, but I guess it's going to work.
The only thing is that I couldn't extract the quantile. For the soil, as I am considering the area around the plot, the mean or median might be good. However, for canopy height, the quantile 90 would be more suitable.
I'm using the tutorial script as a base, but it's giving a problem in the "extract" function. The full script I'm using is attached.

## Extracting the estimate plant height at 10% and 90% of quantile:

EPH.Extract<-extract(x=DSM.P$newMosaic, y=Shapefile$fieldShape)

Error in Use Method(“extract”) :

                No applicable method for “extract” applied to an object of class “c(“RasterStack”, “Raster”, “TasterStackBrick”, “ BasicRaster”)”

Error: 1 components of “…” were not used.

We detected these problematic arguments:

* “y”

Did you misspecify an argument?

I found it weird because it worked with "fieldInfo" function.

EPH.M <- fieldInfo(DSM.P$newMosaic, fieldShape = Shapefile$fieldShape, fun = "mean")

EPH.M$plotValue

I found it weird because it worked with "fieldInfo" function. I also try to create a function "quantile 90" and use it in the fieldInfo function, "fun="q90", but it didn't work as well.

q90 <- function(x) {quantile(x, probs=0.9)
}

I know you're all super busy, but if someone has already had this problem and know how to solve it, let me know. I'll also keep trying and I'll let you know if I figure it out.

ortho & DEM I'm using: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1bsY7rC-uccfazbPhssi8NrQZnt0Dx5U7?usp=sharing

Best wishes,

Cleber
